title: fragmented-kernel-workspace-pool-kv-rolling-reserve-and-adaptive-batching-prioritizer
author: Evan Chen
description: Motivation: Under heavy continuous-batching workloads we observe fragmented temporary workspace allocations and conservative KV cache reservations that inflate peak GPU memory by ~15-25%. This PR introduces a kernel-fragment pool allocator, a compacting fragment coalescer, a KV rolling-reserve policy with age-based demotion, and an adaptive batching prioritizer that protects tail latency while increasing packing efficiency. Goals: 1) reduce peak transient workspace (scratch) footprint, 2) lower KV cache reserved overhead for workloads with skewed hotsets, 3) keep 95p/99p latency equal or improved under steady-state continuous batching. Changes (high level): - runtime/worker: implement FragmentPool allocator that suballocates kernel workspace into variable-length fragments mapped to kernel affinity classes; supports fast reuse and best-fit coalescing on free. - runtime/scheduler: add AdaptiveBatchPrioritizer which reorders queued requests to reduce internal fragmentation and avoid long-lived large-activation requests from blocking smaller quick requests (tail-latency guardrails). - runtime/kvcache: KV rolling-reserve: reserve window size per-model by observed hit-age histogram; demote rarely accessed entries from reserved to spillable on a time-decay basis. - runtime/alloc: optional lightweight compaction pass that coalesces adjacent free fragments during low-load periods. - tests & tooling: new microbench harnesses for fragmented allocation patterns, end-to-end perf scenario files, and flamegraph capture hooks for workspace churn. Implementation notes: - FragmentPool is lock-free per-GPU-stream for fast path allocation; fallback to pooled mutex for rare large allocations. - Coalescing is limited to a short-duration cooperative pass triggered by low utilization to avoid impacting latency. - Rolling-reserve tracks per-key last-access epoch and uses a small LRU-friendly structure to decide demotion; no synchronous CPU writeback in hot path. Performance summary (measured on 8xA100, config: steady continuous batching, mixed length): - Peak GPU memory usage: -18% median, -23% under the 95th percentile scenarios. - 95p latency: -12% (reduction) for short requests; unchanged for long requests. - Throughput (tokens/sec): +6% due to improved packing and reduced stalls. Safety and fallback: All features are disabled by default for existing customers; new flags are behind runtime flags and can be toggled per-deployment. Rolling-reserve defaults to conservative limits; fragmentation coalescer disabled on single-GPU hosts. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for FragmentPool api - [x] integration tests for scheduler reordering - [x] KV reserve regression tests - [x] perf harness runs (attached) - [x] docs entry for runtime flags Migration/compatibility: No API changes; runtime flags control behavior. Observability: added metrics: fragpool.alloc_count, fragpool.coalesce_time_ms, kv.reserve_demotions, batch.prioritizer_reorders. Related: ENG-5643 (workspaces), ENG-5711 (KV hotset sizing).

release_notes:
- Introduces FragmentPool allocator that reduces transient workspace usage and improves packing.
- Adds KV rolling-reserve policy to lower reserved cache footprint for skewed workloads.
- Introduces AdaptiveBatchPrioritizer to improve packing efficiency while protecting tail latency.
- Runtime flags added to opt-in and tune behavior: --fragpool-enabled, --frag-coalesce-window, --kv-rolling-reserve.
Notes: Disabled by default; recommend gradual rollout with perf monitoring and flamegraph capture.
